text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The agricultural and forestry ministry, which has a 27.2 percent stake in the Panevezhys Sema spirits producer, vetoed the company's plan to issue a new 18 million share emmission abroad. Brokerage house Vilfima was preparing the project for London investment house Williams de Broe.
- Two thousand soldiers will participate in the six day military training exercise Spring winds which begins today near Panevezhys.

- The World Bank will issue a credit to reform Lithuania's health care system in 1999, one year later than originally expected, health care minister Juozas Galdikas said on Monday after his trip to Washington.
- Vilniaus Bank's net profit rose sharply to 24.4 million litas in 1996 versus 2.9 million litas the previous year.
- Fifteen passengers were injured in a trolleybus accident in Vilnius on Monday.
- Lithuania's social security and pensions fund owes the country's drug stores 48.7 million litas.
- The board of Vilniaus bank will recommend to the bank's shareholders that most of the 1996 profit be retained within the company.
- Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas' advisors deny that there is any conflict between the president and parliament.
